paragraphs.text: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, began trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday, November 19, 2026, under the ticker ANT. Its first trade came in at $111.50 a share, according to CNBC and CNN, about 34 percent above the $83 price the company set for its initial public offering the night before.

Before the open, indications pointed to a strong start. Reuters reported that as of 11:38 a.m. Eastern time, shares were expected to begin trading at $110.50, about 33 percent above the offer price, and that Anthropic was on track to be valued at more than $2 trillion.

Anthropic priced the offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, November 18, above the marketed range of $70 to $78, according to Trending Topics and IBTimes. The company sold 980 million Class A shares and raised about $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record. Most of the shares were newly issued, and the rest were sold by the company's seven co-founders.

A separate private placement of $26 billion, led by Nvidia and Google, brought the total size of the deal to about $107.3 billion, Trending Topics reported, citing the company's figures. Demand for the IPO was strong: orders came in at about seven times the number of shares on offer, according to Bloomberg reporting cited by Trending Topics.

Anthropic's growth is the main reason for the demand. Yahoo Finance reported that the company's revenue in the third quarter was about $17 billion, up roughly 12 times from a year earlier, and that sales for the first nine months of 2026 passed $33 billion.

Chief executive Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei, the siblings who co-founded the company in 2021, rang the opening bell at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York along with colleagues. Reuters reported that Dario Amodei and six co-founders together own roughly 10 percent of Anthropic, and calculated their combined stakes at nearly $150 billion based on the IPO price, before the first day gain.
In an interview with CNBC cited by Reuters, Dario Amodei said Anthropic may borrow in the future, saying the company hopes to be investment grade and that debt is an instrument available to it.

Most shareholders are locked up for 180 days, and the co-founders and some large holders for up to a year, according to Trending Topics, which also reported that activists protested outside the Nasdaq tower in Times Square over risks to pension money.

Not every investor is convinced. Bill Gunderson of GCG Advisory Partners told Reuters that Anthropic is a one-trick pony and needs to reach profitability soon. Lukas Muehlbauer of IPOX said some of the demand may come from investors who do not want to miss a rare opportunity rather than from confidence in long term profits.

A first trade this far above the offer price shows how much public investors want direct exposure to a frontier AI lab, a chance that until now was limited to private funds and a few large tech partners. It also sets a high bar. At these prices, Anthropic will be judged every quarter on whether its revenue growth continues and whether it can turn that growth into profit.
Watch where ANT closes on its first day and how the stock behaves as the 180 day lockup approaches, since that is when many early holders will be free to sell.
